original_test_intent: Factory-reset the intended BMC through the approved in-band OEM path, prove the documented configuration/NVRAM reset scope and re-establish required management service without losing recoverability or misreporting unaffected data.
original_method: Master specifies OEM 0x30/0x41 with an Ethernet Interface Select. Review preserves it but rejects log clearing, selector omission, fixed-sleep readiness and command-success-only acceptance.
manual_activity: Owner/vendor defines exactly which BMC settings, credentials, network, inventory and logs reset or persist, supplies a dedicated target, verified backup/reconfiguration package and independent OOB/console recovery, then authorizes one reset.
required_inputs: Current network, users, security, FRU, SDR, SEL and host-power state
Complete configuration backup and integrity check
Known post-reset credentials and network bootstrap
Maintenance window and fresh explicit approval
safety_requirements: Do not clear logs before reset
Do not use sshpass or disable host-key verification
Do not omit or guess selector
Validate backup and recovery before confirmation
Do not use fixed sleep as readiness proof
Do not auto-retry or power-cycle host/BMC
Stop on identity/access/scope discrepancy and preserve evidence
agent_execution_scope: Verify BMC/host/firmware and independent recovery path
Capture and hash complete approved pre-state/backup
Validate vendor selector, reset scope and readiness sequence
Present destructive scope for fresh confirmation
Poll only documented bounded readiness states
Compare every scoped configuration and preservation field
engineer_actions: Approve target, scope, backup, downtime and recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unsafe: it omits the selector, exposes credentials, disables host verification and assumes ten seconds plus mc info proves a recoverable factory reset.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Only after fresh destructive-action confirmation, issue protected `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x41 <validated-Ethernet-Interface-Select>` once, then follow the firmware-defined readiness and recovery runbook; never auto-repeat.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 0x30/0x41 family, selector placeholder and 10/5 timing remain preserved; no reset scope, delay or recovery step is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Back up and verify the full scoped BMC state on a dedicated recoverable target, confirm one factory reset, track documented readiness, restore access/configuration and compare the observed default/preserved state to the vendor matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the essential destructive-action, backup, readiness, recovery and state-comparison controls without altering Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: mc info or restored connectivity alone does not prove documented factory defaults, preservation rules or complete management recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Factory reset can remove credentials, network/security policy and NVRAM configuration, interrupt management and require independent recovery; an undocumented scope can make rollback impossible.

project_override_considerations: A vendor UI/API reset is equivalent only when its exact scope matches 0x30/0x41, readiness and state comparison are recorded, and the untested original in-band method is disclosed.
expected_evidence: Verified dedicated target/firmware and reset-scope matrix
Configuration backup hashes and independent recovery proof
Documented readiness timeline without fixed-sleep assumption
Post-reset identity, firmware, users/security/network, FRU/SDR/SEL and host-power matrix
No retry and preserved diagnostic audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source performs a destructive factory reset but clears evidence and defines PASS only as no error/reset. DeepSeek omits the selector, uses insecure access and a fixed sleep plus mc info. These do not establish the actual reset scope or recovery.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The destructive objective is explicit. Vendor scope, backup, dedicated environment, readiness and recovery are stringent project execution inputs; review can complete while execution remains prohibited until they are satisfied.

review_improvement: Defines the destructive scope, backup integrity, independent recovery, bounded readiness and field-by-field post-reset verification while banning automatic retry and implicit host power action.
independent_technical_reasoning: Factory reset is not validated by command completion or BMC responsiveness. Its correctness is the set difference between fields documented to default and fields documented to persist, plus successful restoration of management access. Because the command can erase the very credentials and network path used to observe it, verification and recovery must exist independently before execution; a fixed sleep is neither readiness detection nor a recovery plan.
